title: Publish-path credential inventory: quest resolves the SAME Keychain item as lore, and no release record names the auth source a publish used
description:
Routed by opum-agent 2026-09-15 17:50Z and corrected by it and lore-cli at 18:00Z. An npm publish token is reported exposed 2026-09-14 (lore-cli LCLI-500); lore-cli first claimed the publishing credential is shared with quest, then withdrew that as unverified and asked quest to measure its own path. THE EXPOSURE ITSELF IS UNVERIFIED HERE -- it reaches this repository only as a secondhand summary of another repo task, and nothing below confirms an exposure occurred or which credential it was.

MEASURED HERE, in this repository, no credential value printed at any point:

1. scripts/publish-release.mjs resolves auth in strict precedence Keychain -> $NPM_TOKEN -> interactive npm login (lines 110-123). KEYCHAIN_SERVICE is "npm-opum-ai-publish" (line 65).
2. It NEVER reads ~/.npmrc. It writes the token to a temp npmrc and sets npm_config_userconfig for the run, leaving ~/.npmrc untouched (lines 11-12, 286-289).
3. `security find-generic-password -s npm-opum-ai-publish` returns svce=npm-opum-ai-publish acct=jdnewhouse. The item exists, so the local path resolves the Keychain and never falls through.
4. The script ALREADY prints what lore-cli recommends adding: line 280 emits `Auth: using a token from ${source} (length=... prefix=... whitespace=...)`, shape only, no value.

CONCLUSION ON COUPLING, which runs OPPOSITE to the 18:00Z correction: the correction argued that multiple live credentials make sharing less likely. That reasoning is sound and its conclusion does not survive the measurement. lore resolves Keychain first with the entry present, and quest resolves the same service name first with the entry present, so both publish on the same Keychain ITEM -- not merely the same npm account. The ~/.npmrc tokens are irrelevant to both, because neither path reads that file. One step is still secondhand: I read quest KEYCHAIN_SERVICE constant myself, and take lore service name from opum-agent measurement naming that exact service while describing lore path. lore-cli should confirm its own constant before this is treated as settled.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR A ROTATION: the stranding risk lore-cli raised is smaller than feared, in this direction -- jeremy-newhouse is sole owner of both packages, so replacing the Keychain item VALUE keeps both publishing. The real hazard is the opposite: revoking an old token without replacing the item, or revoking one of the other credentials on the machine, leaves the exposure open and breaks publishing.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT PATH: .github/workflows/release.yml publishes from CI with `id-token: write` and a stored NPM_TOKEN secret (lines 44, 55, 163-182). A Keychain rotation does not cover it. So "rotate the npm token" does not name a single object for this repository either, for a different reason than it failed to for lore.

THE GAP WORTH FIXING REGARDLESS: grepping .quest/ for "Auth: using a token from" returns nothing. The script prints the auth source on every run and no release record captures it, so nobody can now say which credential 0.7.0 or 0.7.1 actually went out on. Printing it is not the same as retaining it -- that is lore-cli LCLI-488 finding carried one step further.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The repository publish paths are inventoried in writing and the count is right: ONE rotation surface, the Keychain item npm-opum-ai-publish acct jdnewhouse, resolved by scripts/publish-release.mjs. CI publishes by OIDC trusted publishing with no stored secret (gh secret list empty), and the two ~/.npmrc tokens are read by neither path
lore-cli has confirmed its own KEYCHAIN_SERVICE constant first-hand, closing the one secondhand step in the same-item claim

release.yml gains a guard that FAILS the publish job when a registry auth token is configured, so the safe state is enforced rather than merely current -- quest reaches it today by having no secret and unsetting NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, and nothing would notice a secret added later

The publish procedure records the auth source line the script already prints (publish-release.mjs:280) onto the release task, so a later rotation can name the credential a given version went out on instead of inferring it forward from present configuration
The rotation decision is this repository own user, taken with these measurements attached and not inherited from lore-cli user

implementationNotes:
CORRECTION, self-inflicted, and it removes a whole rotation surface I had reported to two peers. I claimed .github/workflows/release.yml publishes with a stored NPM_TOKEN secret. It does not. I read line 44, which is a COMMENT explaining why trusted publishing is used -- it says a stored NPM_TOKEN "return[s] E404 on PUT" as historical justification -- and treated a sentence about a token as a reference to one. This repository own CLAUDE.md warns about exactly this shape (read the assertion, never the sentence above it) and I did it anyway.

Measured properly:
- `gh secret list --repo opum-ai/quest-cli` returns EMPTY. No repository secrets are configured at all.
- The only `secrets.*` reference in any workflow is `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` (release.yml:94, prepublication-qualification.yml:169), which GitHub provides automatically.
- release.yml:134 and :175 run `unset NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` immediately before each publish invocation, deliberately.

So CI publishes by OIDC trusted publishing only, and the rotation surface is ONE object, not two: the Keychain item. The `~/.npmrc` tokens are read by neither path.

ON opum-agent RELAYED FALLBACK ANALYSIS (17:55Z, lore-cli first-hand on its own repo): the analysis is right and this repository already documents it more precisely than the relay did. release.yml:151-168 carries a correction lore-cli itself made on 2026-09-13 from npm own source -- publish.js calls oidc() unconditionally BEFORE getCredentialsByURI reads any stored token, and oidc.js has no early return on an existing NODE_AUTH_TOKEN (verified byte-identical in npm 11.19.1 and 12.0.2). The exchange is always attempted; oidc() swallows a failure at log.verbose and falls back to whatever .npmrc holds. So a stored token does change what a FAILED exchange does, exactly as relayed.

THE GAP THAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION: quest reaches the safe state by having no secret and unsetting the env var, but nothing ENFORCES it. lore-cli fails the job if a registry auth token is configured (their publish job, lines 783-791). Quest has no such guard, so a secret added later would silently restore the fallback and no gate would notice. That guard is worth stealing on its own merits and does not depend on any rotation decision.

USER RULING 2026-09-15: DEFER. Asked directly with the measurements attached (AskUserQuestion, two options: rotate now, or defer and match lore-cli). The user chose to defer and match lore-cli, whose own user deferred for the third time the same day and published 0.7.0 on the current token.

Recorded so the next session does not re-litigate it from scratch: the deferral is this repository own user decision of 2026-09-15, not an inheritance of lore-cli user call, and it covers the Keychain item npm-opum-ai-publish. It is not a ruling on the guard in criterion 3, which is a workflow hardening independent of any rotation and was not put to the user.

Nothing is pending to publish here -- dev is past v0.7.1 with no src/ or package.json change -- so the deferral strands no release. The exposure itself remains UNVERIFIED in this repository: it arrives only as a secondhand summary of lore-cli LCLI-500, and nothing measured here confirms an exposure occurred or which credential it was. Whoever revisits this should establish that first.
